title: First white jazz band he heard: the High Rollers
summary: He recalls hearing the High Rollers, a white ragtime band, around 1908; the word jazz was then a bad word.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: That was the final. Well, from those early days then, they had, did they have white musicians playing what today we could have called early jazz? They had white musicians. The boys? At the turn of the century now we're talking about, they had white musicians playing jazz then. Now what were they called?

Well, now I can tell you about, let's see, 1905. No, I would say from about 1908 or something like that. Because what do I remember, I couldn't be no more than about nine or ten years old at the time. When I heard the first, when I heard the first jazz band, white jazz band, and that was the High Rollers. High Rollers? High Rollers.

That only came out lately, it was jazz. Because, to tell you the truth, at that time, if you said a word of jazz in front of women folks, they'd knock your head off. Bad word.
